questions.question: Why does TR27 use the term "product package" instead of the older term "container/closure system"?

options.A: Because the new term is limited to glass vials with rubber stoppers, and "package seal" refers specifically to the crimping of the rubber stopper and aluminum cap
options.B: Because the new term covers any non-porous barrier system that protects a drug product from its environment, and "package seal" refers generically to any type of seal
options.C: Because the new term refers only to empty containers shipped by the packaging supplier, excluding the filled finished product, and does not involve sealing
options.D: Because the new term excludes sterile products so the guidance can apply to all non-sterile dosage forms, and the definition of seal is dropped

questions.explanation: TR27 explains that "product package" covers any non-porous barrier system that protects a drug product from its environment, and "package seal" refers generically to all types of seals or closures. Although the document is written for all dosage forms, its focus is explicitly on sterile product packaging, so the statement that sterile products are excluded is the reverse of the truth.

questions.question: Which statement about the nature and predecessor of TR27 is correct?

options.A: It is a mandatory standard that completely replaces the relevant USP chapters and has regulatory force
options.B: It is PDA's interpretation of regulations, carries the weight of an implied compliance standard, and can be cited directly during inspections
options.C: It is a reference guide that does not establish a mandatory or implied standard and supersedes PDA TIB No. 4
options.D: It is PDA's first package integrity document, and no related bulletin or technical report existed before it

questions.explanation: The TR27 preface states explicitly that the document should be regarded as a guide, not intended to establish any mandatory or implied standard, and that it supersedes the earlier PDA Technical Information Bulletin No. 4 (Aspects of Container/Closure Integrity). The statements of a mandatory standard and an implied compliance standard are both contrary to its positioning as a guide.

questions.topic: What package integrity assurance is about
questions.question: According to the TR27 introduction, what is package integrity assurance mainly concerned with?

options.A: Containment of the product within the package and effective exclusion of microorganisms and reactive gases, sometimes with maintenance of a vacuum
options.B: Whether the package looks attractive, the labeling is clear, and the opening method is convenient for patients
options.C: The cost of packaging materials, supply stability, and shipping efficiency and storage conditions during logistics
options.D: Only protection of the product from light, to prevent degradation of the active ingredient on exposure, unrelated to gases or microorganisms

questions.explanation: The introduction lists many functions of a container (such as ease of use, prevention of misuse, and light protection), but integrity assurance is mainly concerned with containment of the product and effective exclusion of microorganisms and reactive gases (such as oxygen and water vapor), and sometimes with maintenance of a vacuum. Light protection is just one of the container's functions and not the core of integrity assurance.

questions.question: A sterile drug manufacturer that has produced commercially for years must change the stopper material because its supplier has changed. Under TR27, how should package integrity be handled?

options.A: No reassessment is needed as long as the stopper still meets incoming specifications, since integrity was already confirmed at commercialization
options.B: Only increase the number of sterility test samples at finished product release, using the larger sample as evidence of package integrity
options.C: Wait until the next routine stability study to assess it, without starting a separate change assessment
options.D: Package integrity should be reconfirmed, because a significant change in design, materials, or process conditions (including sterilization) calls for reconfirmation

questions.explanation: TR27 states that integrity assessment runs through the entire product life cycle, and that further reconfirmation should be carried out when there are significant changes to the package system that could affect integrity (package design, packaging materials) or when manufacturing conditions (including sterilization) change. The sterility test is not a reliable indicator of integrity, so increasing the number of sterility test samples is not a workable approach.

questions.question: TR27 explains that one needs to understand the seal locations and sealing mechanisms and to test the package and process parameters under extreme conditions. Which phase of the product life cycle does this belong to?

options.A: The package design, process development, and robustness assessment phase (3.1)
options.B: The in-process control and continuous monitoring phase during commercial production (3.2)
options.C: The finished product testing and batch release phase (3.3)
options.D: The post-marketing change management and annual review phase

questions.explanation: The overview of Section 3 states that during package design and process development, the seal locations, the sealing mechanisms, and the critical factors in design, assembly, and processing that can affect seal quality must be well understood, and the package must be tested under extreme conditions to ensure it can withstand processing, shipping, and use. In-process control and finished product testing apply only after commercialization.

questions.question: TR27 defines seal and closure separately. Which statement about a sterile glass vial sealed with an elastomeric stopper is correct?

options.A: It is a seal, because two materials are joined by adhesive or heat fusion, forming an irreversible continuous interface
options.B: It is a seal, because the stopper and vial finish are heat-fused into one piece and the leak rate depends on bond strength
options.C: It is a closure (two surfaces in physical contact); the viscoelasticity of the stopper lets it conform to the vial surface under compression, and the leak rate can be very low
options.D: It is a closure, but depends entirely on a tortuous path for its barrier, regardless of material elasticity or degree of compression

questions.explanation: A seal is a bond between two surfaces (such as an ampoule, a heat-sealed pouch, or a joint made with adhesive), while a closure is a physical contact between two surfaces. A stoppered vial is a closure; the viscoelasticity of the stopper allows it to conform to the vial surface under compression, achieving a very low gas leak rate, and it does not rely only on a tortuous path.

questions.question: Which statement about TR27's description of in-process control and in-line leak detection is correct?

options.A: As long as the in-line leak detection instrument is fast enough and sensitive enough, it can replace monitoring and recording of sealing parameters
options.B: The purpose of in-line leak detection instruments is to measure the permeation rate of gas through the packaging material itself, not to find sporadic leaks
options.C: In-process control relies mainly on the performance of the final product rather than on individual unit operation performance or process parameters
options.D: In-line leak detection is used to find sporadic gross-leak packages that bypassed in-process controls, and cannot replace control of critical sealing parameters

questions.explanation: TR27 explains that in-line leak detection instruments are designed to detect sporadic defective units that bypassed process controls and leak at larger rates, and that no in-line instrument is currently designed to measure gas permeation. No amount of in-line or finished product inspection can replace control and monitoring of critical package and seal parameters; the criteria for in-process control are typically based on unit operation performance.

questions.question: Why does TR27 consider the sterility test no longer a reliable final indicator of package integrity?

options.A: Because the sterility test can be performed only on opened products and cannot be run on intact packages
options.B: Because the sterility test lacks sensitivity, uses few samples, and can give false positives
options.C: Because the sterility test cannot be run on liquid products and is suitable only for solid dosage forms
options.D: Because regulations expressly prohibit release on the basis of sterility testing, and parametric release is the only route

questions.explanation: TR27 states that the sterility test was historically used as an indicator of package integrity, but because the method is insensitive, tests very few samples, and can yield false positives, it is no longer considered a reliable final indicator. The other options are not mentioned in the text.

questions.question: In the leak rate unit conversions mentioned in TR27, 1 Pa·m³/s is approximately equal to how many std cc/s?

options.A: About 10 std cc/s (exact value 9.87)
options.B: About 1 std cc/s (exact value 1.01, nearly equal)
options.C: About 0.1 std cc/s (exact value 0.0987, about one tenth)
options.D: About 100 std cc/s (exact value 98.7, about one hundred times)

questions.explanation: TR27 states that 1 Pa·m³/s equals 9.87 std cc/s, or about 10 std cc/s. Std cc/s (or scc/s) is the volume of gas passing through a defect per second under standard conditions; atm cc/s is not exactly the same but is often used interchangeably.

questions.topic: Test method sensitivity: more than one method
questions.question: What is the main reason a product/package system sometimes needs more than one leak test method?

options.A: Because regulations require every product to undergo both physical and microbiological tests and compare the results
options.B: Because a single method is too costly, so testing must be shared across several laboratories to reduce each laboratory's equipment investment
options.C: Because most physical methods each have an optimal sensitivity range, and the leak size of concern differs between life-cycle stages
options.D: Because a highly sensitive method is always more suitable than a less sensitive one, so several methods are needed to cross-verify each other

questions.explanation: TR27 explains that most methods have an optimal sensitivity range and that the leak size of concern differs at different stages. For example, with lyophilized powder, shipping simulation looks for larger leaks caused by vibration and shock, while long-term stability samples are checked for gas leakage and permeation. A more sensitive method is not necessarily better; excessive sensitivity is both inappropriate and expensive.

questions.topic: When to choose a microbial challenge test
questions.question: A package relies entirely on a tortuous path to exclude airborne microorganisms, and no reliable physical method can test it. Under TR27, what is the most reasonable approach?

options.A: Substitute helium mass spectrometry, the most sensitive method, and infer microbial ingress directly from its leak rate
options.B: Perform no integrity assessment, because this type of package inherently does not need to demonstrate integrity
options.C: Rely only on finished product sterility test results, using the pass rate of released batches as evidence
options.D: Use a microbial challenge test, because such packages may have no reasonable physical alternative

questions.explanation: TR27 lists, among the reasons for choosing a microbial challenge test, that some closures or packages that rely only on a tortuous path to exclude airborne microorganisms may not be reliably testable by physical methods, so no reasonable alternative exists. The sterility test is not considered a reliable integrity indicator.

questions.topic: When a physical test is preferred
questions.question: Under what circumstances does TR27 consider a physical test a more reasonable choice than a microbial challenge test?

options.A: The leak rate specification is far below the microbial ingress limit, as for a sterile glass vial that must maintain an inert gas headspace
options.B: The company lacks the resources, equipment, and expertise needed to develop and validate physical methods
options.C: The package cannot withstand the higher pressure differential or vacuum required for physical testing and is easily damaged
options.D: The product is distributed only in small quantities and does not justify the full validation and equipment cost of a physical method

questions.explanation: A physical test is the more reasonable choice when the leak rate specification is clearly below the limit for microbial ingress. For example, a stoppered vial that must maintain an inert gas headspace has a specification tighter than the helium leak rate for liquid microbial ingress (about 10^-5 std cc/s), so a microbial challenge test is not needed. The other situations described (lack of resources, a package that cannot withstand physical testing, small-volume distribution) are in fact among the reasons TR27 lists for choosing a microbial challenge test.

questions.question: Which statement is correct under TR27's recommendations for liquid immersion microbial challenge tests?

options.A: A standardized immersion test method exists and can simply be followed, with no need to design the conditions yourself
options.B: If more than one seal is relied on, each seal should be challenged
options.C: Larger bacteria should be chosen so that ingress is easier to observe
options.D: The positive control need only use intact packages and does not require samples with defects

questions.explanation: TR27 notes that there is no standard liquid immersion test and recommends the following: select small bacteria that reach a high viable count at the end of the test, include a positive control (such as a defective package) that demonstrates growth, use a statistically representative number of samples, and challenge each seal if more than one seal is relied on. Intact packages cannot serve as a positive control demonstrating growth.

questions.question: A laboratory wants to replace a microbial test with a new physical leak method. Rather than microbially challenging packages, it demonstrates that the new method can reliably detect leak rates (about 10^-5 std cc/s measured with helium) or smaller that the literature has shown to permit microbial ingress. What kind of approach is this?

options.A: Direct correlation, because the same lot of packages has undergone both physical and microbial testing
options.B: In-process control, because it only monitors unit operation performance and does not involve leak rates
options.C: Indirect correlation, comparing method sensitivity with documented leak rates that permit ingress
options.D: No correlation approach at all, because physical methods cannot be linked to microbial ingress and can only be used independently

questions.explanation: Direct correlation requires the same lot of packages to undergo both physical and microbial testing, with the relationship between leak rate and probability of microbial failure established quantitatively. Indirect correlation compares the detection capability of the physical method with documented leak rates at which microbial ingress occurs; because the gas, temperature, and pressure differential of the reference test and the new method may differ, conversion to an equivalent leak rate may be needed.

questions.question: When using the TR27 decision tree, to which seal type does an ampoule formed in one piece from a single material (such as glass or plastic) belong?

options.A: Compression or friction fit closure
options.B: Thermal or adhesive bond
options.C: Tortuous path dependent closure
options.D: Contiguous container

questions.explanation: The decision tree's glossary defines a package formed from a single material (such as a glass or plastic ampoule) as a contiguous container. An example of a compression or friction fit is a rubber stopper in a glass vial; thermal or adhesive bonds include heat-sealed plastic laminates; and tortuous path closures include crimped aluminum tubes or screw-thread closures.

questions.question: Helium mass spectrometry has four test modes. According to TR27, which two can provide quantitative results?

options.A: Tracer Probe and Detector Probe
options.B: Hood and Inside-Out
options.C: Tracer Probe and Hood
options.D: Detector Probe and Inside-Out

questions.explanation: TR27 states that of the four helium mass spectrometry modes, Hood and Inside-Out are quantitative, while Tracer Probe and Detector Probe are qualitative or semi-quantitative. In Tracer Probe, helium is sprayed on the outside of the package; in Detector Probe, a probe samples the gas around the package.

questions.question: Which product/package combination best meets the applicability conditions for HVLD (high voltage leak detection)?

options.A: A non-conductive container holding a liquid product of significantly higher conductivity, with the product able to reach the potential leak site
options.B: A conductive metal container holding a non-conductive oily product, with an air gap that must be kept between the product and the electrode
options.C: A liquid-free dry powder package relying on a tortuous path closure, with an insulating outer shell
options.D: A container of any material, as long as it can withstand vacuum, regardless of product conductivity or liquid content

questions.explanation: HVLD applies only to containers of relatively non-conductive material, with a product of significantly higher conductivity, and the product must be at or near the leak site to conduct. TR27 also recommends evaluating the effect of the voltage on product stability; the method is qualitative, and the test is virtually instantaneous.

questions.question: A sterile package relies on a tortuous path or barrier seal and cannot withstand liquid immersion. Which microbial challenge method is more suitable, and what is the typical challenge organism?

options.A: Liquid immersion challenge, using Escherichia coli
options.B: Liquid immersion challenge, using Brevundimonas diminuta with 7-14 days of incubation
options.C: Aerosol microbial challenge (aerosolization), typically using B. subtilis spores
options.D: Particulate penetration test, using carbon black or talc as the challenge material

questions.explanation: The aerosol challenge applies to sterile packages that cannot withstand liquid immersion and rely on a tortuous path or barrier seal, and the typical challenge organism is B. subtilis spores. Liquid immersion is for packages that can withstand immersion and is typically incubated for 7-14 days. Particulate penetration uses dust rather than microorganisms and cannot directly demonstrate microbial ingress.

questions.question: A lot of vacuum-sealed packages needs rapid in-line screening for inadequate vacuum. Which method best matches the TR27 description?

options.A: Bubble test, immersing the package in water under vacuum and watching for continuous bubbles, readable within minutes
options.B: Liquid tracer test, using dye immersion for several hours and reading dye ingress visually or by spectrophotometer
options.C: Weight loss/gain test, tracking package weight changes over days to weeks to determine gas or moisture permeation
options.D: Residual gas ionization, applying a high-voltage, high-frequency electric field to the vacuum-sealed package, with a decision in under one second

questions.explanation: Residual gas ionization applies a high-voltage, high-frequency electric field to the vacuum-sealed package to ionize the residual gas; a conductive plate detects the ionization current, and a value above the set limit fails the package. Test time is under one second, and the method is qualitative. The package itself must be relatively resistant to ionization, and the effect of electrical sparking on product stability should be considered.

questions.question: Which statement about the lid deflection test is correct?

options.A: It is a quantitative measurement of gas leak rate, with sensitivity at the level of helium mass spectrometry, and can replace helium leak testing
options.B: It is usually an indicator of larger leaks and is often paired with pressure/vacuum decay to cover both the gross and fine ranges
options.C: It requires immersing the package in dye and measuring the amount of dye entering the package with a spectrophotometer to determine leak size
options.D: It applies only to packages with tortuous path closures and not to elastomeric stoppers or heat-sealed packages

questions.explanation: Lid deflection applies a pressure differential to the package and monitors movement of a flexible lid to detect leaks; it is a qualitative method, usually an indicator of larger leaks, and is often paired with pressure/vacuum decay to cover both the gross and fine detection ranges. It applies to packages that do not rely on a tortuous path or barrier seal and that can withstand a pressure differential.

questions.topic: ASTM standards in the reference list
questions.question: Among the ASTM test methods in the TR27 reference list, which one performs leak testing by the bubble emission technique?

options.A: ASTM E 515-94
options.B: ASTM E 165-94
options.C: ASTM E 493-94
options.D: ASTM E 1002-94

questions.explanation: E 515-94 tests for leaks by the bubble emission technique and corresponds to the bubble test. E 165-94 is liquid penetrant examination; E 493-94 uses a mass spectrometer leak detector in inside-out mode; and E 1002-94 is ultrasonic leak testing.

questions.question: TR27 cites in several places the three 1997 papers by Kirsch et al. titled "Pharmaceutical container/closure integrity." Which one examines the relationship between microbial ingress and helium leak rate in rubber-stoppered glass vials?

options.A: Part I: mass-spectrometer-based helium leak rate detection in rubber-stoppered glass vials
options.B: Part III: validation of the helium leak rate method in rigid pharmaceutical containers
options.C: Part II: the relationship between microbial ingress and helium leak rate in rubber-stoppered glass vials
options.D: All three discuss only the equipment specifications and calibration of helium mass spectrometers and do not address microbial ingress

questions.explanation: The three 1997 papers by Kirsch et al. are, in order: I, mass-spectrometer-based helium leak rate detection in rubber-stoppered glass vials; II, the relationship between microbial ingress and helium leak rate; and III, validation of the helium leak rate method in rigid containers. Part II is the basis TR27 uses to link helium leak rate to microbial ingress (about 10^-5 std cc/s).

questions.question: A company wants a reference document to help it select a leak testing method. Which of the ASTM guides listed in the TR27 references was written for this purpose?

options.A: E 908-91, practice for calibrating gas reference leaks
options.B: E 479-91, guide for preparation of a leak testing specification
options.C: E 1916, terminology for nondestructive examination
options.D: E 432-91, guide for the selection of a leak testing method

questions.explanation: E 432-91 is the Guide for the selection of a leak testing method; E 479-91 is the guide for preparing a leak testing specification; E 908-91 is the practice for calibrating gas reference leaks; and E 1916 is the terminology for nondestructive examination.

questions.question: TR27 cites the paper by Butler et al. (1978) on detecting ampoule leaks with short-half-life radionuclides. Under which method is this reference grouped in the method summaries?

options.A: Helium mass spectrometry, detecting leaks with helium as the tracer gas
options.B: Liquid tracer test
options.C: Microbial challenge test, aerosol method, testing ingress with aerosolized microorganisms
options.D: Weight loss/gain test, measuring weight changes over a long period

questions.explanation: The tracer liquid used in a liquid tracer test may be a dye, a radionuclide, or metal ions, and the Butler et al. radionuclide paper is listed among the references for the liquid tracer method. Helium mass spectrometry uses helium gas, and the other methods listed have nothing to do with radionuclides.

questions.question: The TR27 references list ASTM F1585-95 and F1608-95. What is the difference between them?

options.A: F1585 is microbial ranking of porous packaging materials (exposure chamber method); F1608 is integrity testing for porous barrier medical devices
options.B: Both are bubble test standards, differing only in the container size and seal type to which they apply
options.C: F1585 is integrity testing for porous barrier medical devices; F1608 is microbial ranking of porous packaging materials (exposure chamber method)
options.D: F1585 is a helium mass spectrometry standard and F1608 is a vacuum decay standard, and the two complement each other

questions.explanation: F1585-95 is Integrity testing for porous barrier medical devices; F1608-95 is Microbial ranking of porous packaging materials (exposure chamber method). Both relate to the references for aerosol microbial challenge methods.
